problems.source_says: Not stated. The Study 3 method names no AI tool for the Phase 3 AUT and gives no AI instructions for it. The only AI it describes is the investment advice in the Phase 1 trust game (p. 7). 'Identical to the AUT used in Study 2' can mean the same task (uses for a tennis racket and a water pipe). In Study 2 the two arms got different ChatGPT instructions on the AUT, so the phrase does not say which AI condition each Study 3 cell had. Section 4 never names ChatGPT. The discussion's 'usage style' and 'does not require complete AI abstinence' (p. 12) hint at AI use but do not state it. The form's own reconciliation marks this field confirmed: false and unresolved.

problems.source_says: Not settled by the text. Under the codebook rule the question follows from AI availability while the scored output was produced, and Study 3 does not state it (see the previous problem). If ChatGPT was not available during the Phase 3 AUT, the AUT came after AI exposure in the trust game, and the outcome is after_ai. The ai_design label on the three S3 contrasts would then need review too. If ChatGPT was available, with_ai holds. The supplement's Study 3 task instructions, which this PDF does not include, may settle it.

problems.source_says: Minor. Every number matches Table 4, but only the Model 2 AI-dependence term (B = -1.35, SE = 0.09) is pooled over orientation. Model 3 adds the interaction, with outcome orientation coded 0 and process orientation coded 1 (process B is positive, p. 9, and Table 5 sets W = 0 for outcome). The Model 3 AI-dependence term is therefore the effect under outcome orientation. It matches the outcome-oriented cell gap (2.99 - 4.52 = -1.53), and -1.54 + 0.39 = -1.15 matches the process-oriented gap (4.40 - 5.55). The form's notes say this, but the contrast record files the Model 3 terms under a pooled label.

confirmed: Criterion 3 holds through S2-O1. Three trained raters, blind to condition, scored each AUT response with CAT on novelty, appropriateness, and fluency (7-point scales, ICC = 0.86). The mean of their scores is the creativity index. It is not self-reported. In the high arm much of the scored text is ChatGPT's, adopted as instructed, but it is still each participant's submitted response (p. 6, Section 3.2, Measures; pp. 5-6, procedure).

S2-O1 AI availability is yes, and question is with_ai under the codebook rule. 'Participants in both groups used ChatGPT' in the Phase 2 AUT. The high group was told to adopt ChatGPT's solutions directly, and the low group to use AI only as a supplementary reference. One sentence says the no-tools prohibition was repeated 'again before the creativity task in Phase 2', and the form records this conflict in notes item 10 (pp. 5-6, Section 3.2, Experimental design and procedure).

S2-O1 construct overall_creativity fits. The outcome is one 'creativity index' averaged over raters. The paper reports no dimension-level results (novelty, appropriateness, fluency) and no diversity or within-person variety measure (p. 6, Measures; Table 2).
S2-O1 unit participant is right. Each person has one index, and the arms are compared by independent-samples t-tests with t(130) for 132 people, 66 per group (p. 5, Participants; p. 6, Table 2).

S2-O1 reported numbers match Table 2 and the p. 6 text exactly: High 4.78 (0.66) vs Low 5.20 (0.53), t(130) = 4.03, p < 0.001, d = 0.70, with t and d printed as low minus high in every row. Mediation: c = -0.42, c' = -0.02, ab = -0.40, 95% CI [-0.70, -0.14]. Recomputed from the means and SDs: pooled SD 0.60, d = 0.70, t = 4.03 (p. 6, Table 2 and Mediation analysis).

Measure expert_raters for S2-O1 and S3-O1 is supported by the paper's own label 'expert-rated creativity'. The raters were three psychology graduate students after a 2 h calibration session, so expert vs human raters is a judgment call. Either way the outcome is rated by people, and criterion 3 is unaffected (p. 6, Measures; p. 9, Section 4.3 (2)).

S3-O1 is scored on output by raters. The paper calls it 'expert-rated creativity' on the AUT and says the dependent variable measures were 'the same as in the previous studies' (p. 8, Section 4.2; p. 9, Section 4.3 (2)).

S3-O1 construct overall_creativity, unit participant (Table 4 N = 160, simple-effects t-tests by cell), and timing immediate (single-session procedures) are supported (p. 9, Table 4; p. 13, Section 5.3).

S3-O1 reported numbers match exactly. Table 4 Model 2: AI dependence -1.35*** (0.09), orientation 1.20*** (0.09), R2 0.70, delta R2 0.68***. Model 3: -1.54** (0.13), 1.00*** (0.13), interaction 0.39* (0.18), R2 0.72, delta R2 0.01*. Outcome-oriented cells: 4.52 (1.07) vs 2.99 (0.28), t(77) = 8.87, d = 1.95. Process-oriented cells: 5.55 (0.19) vs 4.40 (0.25), t(77) = 22.70, d = 5.09 (p. 9).

S1-O1 is correctly kept out of scope. It is a 6-item self-report scale that 'captures self-perceived creative capacity across domains rather than performance on a specific creative task'. scored_on_output false, measure self_report, and question none follow the form spec. Its numbers match: r = -0.20, total B = -0.22 (SE 0.09, CI [-0.40, -0.04]), direct B = -0.07 (SE 0.11, p = 0.52), indirect -0.15 (Boot SE 0.06, CI [-0.34, -0.10]) (p. 3, Measures; p. 4, Table 1 and Mediation analysis).

No outcome is missing. The only output-scored outcome in Studies 2 and 3 is the CAT creativity index. Critical thinking, self-efficacy, and the manipulation checks are questionnaires. The paper reports no diversity, similarity, idea count, or unassisted post-AI creative output, and it mentions homogenization only when it cites other work (p. 6, Table 2; pp. 8-10, Tables 3-5; pp. 1 and 11).
summary: Criterion 3 holds: in Study 2, three blind raters scored each participant's AUT response, produced with ChatGPT available in both arms, and S2-O1's construct, unit, question, and Table 2 numbers all check out. The coding is still refuted in detail, because Study 3 never says whether ChatGPT was available during its Phase 3 AUT (so S3-O1's 'yes' and 'with_ai' rest on inference and the outcome could be after_ai), and the first S3 contrast files the Table 4 Model 3 terms, which estimate the effect under outcome orientation, under a pooled label.
